findings.title: Navigation validator is detached from the canonical action/source catalog
findings.evidence: The validator maps Home, Create account and Help to home-library, register and help-desk. Canonical IDs are home, sign-up and help. Its positive unit test directly supplies the invented home-library string, so it does not exercise structured parsing or the actual answer service. The validator also requires app-navigation for every destination even when canonical source bindings are settings-help-menus, account-access, support-status-limits, guide-how-it-works or view-public-debate.
findings.impact: A valid request-local action can be rejected; invented IDs cannot pass normal action membership. Valid Settings and account-access guidance falls back despite having the correct source and action. Several closed destinations remain outside the new check.
findings.minimumCorrection: Derive destination ID, reviewed source binding, audience/applicability and labels from SUPPORT_ACTION_CATALOG and SUPPORT_GUIDE_LABELS rather than a parallel partial table. Require each promised destination to have its exact request-local canonical action and an admitted source binding. Preserve trusted-context and unresolved restrictions.

findings.title: Case/email detector rejects safe ordinary separation prose
findings.evidence: The detector splits on sentence punctuation and semicolon but not comma. “Escalation creates the human case, while support email is a separate mail workflow.” and “Escaladarea creează cazul uman, iar emailul este un flux separat.” each contain EMAIL, CASE and CASE_CREATION in one clause and no literal negation, so both are rejected. Tests use a semicolon that avoids the predicate.
findings.impact: Truthful bilingual public guidance can be silently replaced by fallback solely because of punctuation, weakening free-form answers.
findings.minimumCorrection: Recognize positive separation constructions (while/whereas/separately and Romanian iar/în timp ce/separat) without allowing the unsafe “email creates/opens the case” relation. Add actual answer-service safe and unsafe bilingual cases.
